Top each with a dot of roe.Highland oatcakes and smoked salmonCrisp oatcakes topped with crème fraîche, smoked salmon and dillHow to make it200g rolled oats50g butter, melted100ml crème fraîche150g smoked salmon1 bunch dill1 lemonsalt, to tasteMix the oats with the melted butter, salt and a splash of hot water into a stiff dough.Press thin and cut into rounds.Bake at 180°C for 20 minutes and cool.Top with crème fraîche, smoked salmon, dill and a squeeze of lemon.Shanghai skyline pork belly baoThe glass tower fight in ShanghaiHow to make itAs written, serves 4Fluffy steamed bao stuffed with sticky soy-braised pork belly, quick pickled cucumber, crushed salted peanuts, coriander and a swipe of hoisin.Simmer 800g pork belly, cut into 2cm slices, with 80ml soy, 60ml Shaoxing wine, 3 tbsp brown sugar, sliced ginger and 500ml water for 2 hours until sticky, reducing at the end.Slice a cucumber thin and toss with 2 tbsp rice vinegar and a pinch of sugar for 20 minutes.Steam 12 frozen bao buns for 8 minutes.Fill with hoisin, pork, cucumber, crushed peanuts and coriander.Buttered Arbroath smokie with oatcakesFor M, by the fire, the night before.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsSkyfall lodge venisonJuniper rubbed venison backstrap in whisky redcurrant sauce, with mashHow to make it800g venison backstrap1 tbsp juniper berries, crushed4 sprigs of thyme60ml Scotch whisky2 tbsp redcurrant jelly150ml beef stock600g swede, peeled and chopped50g butter800g potatoes, cut into chunks2 tbsp olive oilsalt and pepper, to tasteRoast the potatoes with the oil at 200°C until golden and crisp.Boil the swede until soft, drain and mash with the butter.Rub the venison with juniper, thyme and pepper. Sear in a hot pan until browned all over, then rest.Add the whisky, redcurrant jelly and stock to the pan and reduce to a glossy sauce.Slice the venison and serve with the mash, potatoes and sauce.Skyfall lodge cullen skinkRigging the lodge before Silva arrivesHow to make itAs written, serves 4Smoked haddock poached in milk and flaked into a thick, creamy potato and leek soup, finished with chives, black pepper and buttered crusty bread.Poach 500g smoked haddock or cod in 750ml milk with a bay leaf for 5 minutes, then lift out and flake, keeping the milk.Soften 2 sliced leeks in 40g butter, add 600g diced potatoes and 400ml water and simmer 15 minutes.Add the milk, mash about half the potatoes to thicken, then add the fish and 100ml cream.Warm through and finish with chives and pepper.Serve with buttered bread.SweetsCranachanWhipped honey whisky cream layered with raspberries and toasted oatsHow to make it60g rolled oats400ml thickened cream3 tbsp honey30ml Scotch whisky300g raspberriesToast the oats in a dry pan until nutty, then cool.Whip the cream with the honey and whisky to soft peaks.Lightly crush the raspberries.Layer cream, raspberries and oats in four glasses, finishing with oats on top.DrinksSilva's island Scotch penicillinScotch, lemon, honey and ginger syrup shaken and served over iceHow to make it60g honey60ml water1 piece ginger, 4cm, sliced200ml blended Scotch whisky80ml lemon juice40ml peated single malt whisky4 large ice cubes4 pieces of candied gingerSimmer the honey, water and sliced ginger for 5 minutes, then cool and strain.Shake the blended Scotch, lemon juice and honey ginger syrup with ice, in batches, and strain over a large ice cube in each tumbler.Float the peated whisky on top and garnish with candied ginger.Fifty year old single maltSilva pours it. Don't stand near the glass.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
